fichas.title: Industrial Buildings: Basics and Planning
fichas.summary: Industrial buildings support the production of goods and may include production buildings, warehouses, technical and administrative buildings, and transport systems. Their design is shaped by production needs, environmental and workplace regulations, fire protection, and product-specific requirements. Layout planning coordinates production and building parameters and informs a scaled room-allocation plan; the resulting design may need to accommodate changing production concepts.
uses: Storage of raw materials and finished products

fichas.title: Life Cycles of Products and Industrial Buildings
fichas.summary: Industrial buildings pass through economic phases analogous to product life cycles. Product cycles may be shorter than the life of a normal building, making adaptability, suitability for letting, and resale value increasingly important. The diagram contrasts product phases with building phases, including rebuilding and demolition.
uses: Adapt to changing economic and product phases

fichas.title: Additive and Integrative Industrial Typologies
fichas.summary: Industrial buildings are classified as additive or integrative plants. Additive plants comprise purpose-shaped functional units arranged in planar or linear structures, often along a production line; units can be extended, developed, or exchanged separately. Integrative plants assemble functional units within a neutral structure to reduce access areas and support reuse, with extension possibilities planned into the building structure.
uses: Arrange production functions in additive or integrated layouts
Enable extension and replacement of functional units
Reduce access areas and support reuse
